subject.size_in_frame: the cake fills the middle band of frame, about 0.34 of frame height; at her size it is a tabletop, and it is composed as one

headroom: the raised glass lid takes the top 0.20 of frame as a bright horizontal slab; below it about 0.10 of clear air, then the cake. The lid pressing down is what keeps the insert inside the box.
horizon_eyeline: Lens at 0.15 m, square-on to the cake so the currant lettering reads flat and level; the cake's surface is a plane running edge to edge across the frame. Her eyeline comes down into the box from above the top edge.

layers.fg: her hands and forearms at the left and right edges, heaving the lid up — the frame is bracketed by her own arms
layers.mg: the cake and the words EAT ME marked in currants, square-on and sharp across their whole width
layers.bg: the inside of the glass box, dark and falling away soft

gaze.note: no face in frame; her presence is carried by the two forearms.

balance: Frontal, centred and symmetrically bracketed by her arms — a small altar composition, which is funny because it is a cake.
leading_lines: The two forearms converge inward from left and right; the lid is a level horizontal above. All three point at the currants.
eye_first: The currants, which is the one legible read they get.
constraint_binding: EAT ME gets exactly one clean legible read here: square-on, sharp across its whole width, held wholly inside title-safe (x 0.36-0.64, y 0.48-0.64). The currants are the only lettering in the shot — no other mark, stamp or inscription appears anywhere in frame. At her size the cake is a tabletop, so it is framed as a horizontal surface she is looking down onto, not as a hand prop.
